catalogue_version: demo-0.1.0 (ILLUSTRATIVE — hand-picked from primary literature, NOT a curated/graded catalogue)
note: Five entries covering exactly the mechanisms confirmed against primary literature while building this profile (see below); not a systematic review of M. abscessus resistance genetics, and no call here has been independently graded the way the WHO Mycobacterium tuberculosis catalogue is. A real deployment needs its own curated review before this profile should inform any decision.
coordinate_note: coordinate_key is absent throughout. erm(41)'s T28/C28 sequevar is encoded by its own gene-relative literature convention (nucleotide 28 of the erm(41) coding sequence), exactly as it is reported in the primary literature, not as a genome coordinate. rrl/rrs positions use the conventional E. coli 23S/16S rRNA numbering that the cited literature itself uses. None of these have been mapped to absolute NZ_CU458896 genome coordinates in this file.
sources: Nash KA, Brown-Elliott BA, Wallace RJ Jr. A novel gene, erm(41), confers inducible macrolide resistance to clinical isolates of Mycobacterium abscessus but is absent from Mycobacterium chelonae. Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 2009;53(4):1367-1376. doi:10.1128/AAC.01275-08

Prammananan T, et al. A single 16S ribosomal RNA substitution is responsible for resistance to amikacin and other 2-deoxystreptamine aminoglycosides in Mycobacterium abscessus and Mycobacterium chelonae. J Infect Dis. 1998;177(6):1573-1581.

Acquired 23S rRNA (rrl) mutations at positions homologous to E. coli A2058/A2059 are widely reported as conferring erm(41)-independent, high-level macrolide resistance in M. abscessus (e.g. Bastian S, et al. Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 2011;55(2):775-781.)

variants.note: Functional 23S rRNA methyltransferase sequevar: inducible macrolide resistance. This is a naturally circulating sequevar, not an acquired mutation from a single reference allele — see coordinate_note.

Non-functional sequevar (Trp10Arg disrupts the methyltransferase): does not confer the inducible-resistance phenotype by itself. Does not by itself establish susceptibility -- other mechanisms (rrl mutation) can still confer resistance.
